question:
Wording check for papertrades.ai (AI paper-trading race with PRETEND money; must never imply real money is involved or that we give advice). A card on the How it works page (and a link to it from the home page) is titled:
"How Season 2 will be closer to real money"
The card explains Season 2 (after Nov 28) adds what real trading would face: bid/ask costs and realistic fills, size limits, borrowing costs and dividends, sharp-move check-ins, a public rule-break counter, an index benchmark after costs. Still pretend money.
The owner asks: should the title say "real trades" (or similar) instead of "real money"?
Options: (1) keep "closer to real money"; (2) "closer to real trading"; (3) "closer to real trades"; (4) another wording you prefer (max 8 words).
Pick one and say why in under 50 words, considering clarity and that "real money" might suggest real money is used.

chatgpt.answer:
Pick (4): “Closer to real-market conditions.”

It points to costs, fills, limits, borrowing, dividends, and benchmarks without implying real money or real execution. It’s clearer and safer than “real money” or “real trades.”

gemini.answer:
I recommend **Option 2: "How Season 2 will be closer to real trading."** 

**Why:** It perfectly captures the new market mechanics (bid/ask, borrow costs, liquidity constraints) without using the word "money." This strictly avoids any dangerous, non-compliant implication that actual funds are deposited or at risk.
